errors.quote: Call **target inhibition** only if target-only orthogonal inhibition is concordant with corrected coupled inhibition and reporter-only/optical-only arms are equivalently clean.
errors.issue: A validated target-only effect can coexist with reporter or optical interference. Requiring clean downstream arms wrongly excludes true target inhibition in mixed cases; earlier text correctly allows mixed effects, so this final classification rule needs revision.

errors.quote: reporter/optical artifacts should not be rescued by target substrate.
errors.issue: Changing target substrate can change intermediate accumulation, reporter saturation, free compound or signal range. Apparent rescue of the coupled assay is not specific for target competition, although the independent target arm mitigates the problem.

errors.quote: If the question requires separating “target binding” from “substrate depletion by compound,”
errors.issue: These chemical-fate/free-substrate controls belong in the core discrimination, not an optional reinterpretation. Product recovery is strong, but substrate availability and tight-binding applicability need explicit verification before target kinetic classification.

rationale: Strong multi-arm study with compound-matched analytical recovery, empirical optical limits, equivalence tests, independent units and a batch-aware analysis. Its final clean-reporter requirement contradicts the recognized possibility of simultaneous mechanisms; substrate rescue is also over-specific. These defects can be repaired without replacing the overall design.
reference_guardrails: D3 establishes spectral proximity, not the magnitude of inner filtering. Fluorophore-only signal loss does not distinguish absorption, quenching and chemical conversion.
Substrate-competitive inhibition is a kinetic subclass of target inhibition; it is not necessarily active-site occupancy. Substrate sequestration and chemical loss require separate controls.
Reporter-only inhibition and true target inhibition can coexist. Do not force mutually exclusive categories or subtract arbitrary effect percentages.

A fully validated staged reporter calibration can be informative; a specific analytical instrument is not mandatory. Target quenching, matrix matching, product recovery and chemical stability must justify the inference.
Orthogonal methods can have their own compound-dependent artifacts, including ion suppression. Nonfluorescence alone does not establish specificity.
Independent preparations/days support reproducibility; technical wells cannot substitute for them. A null significance test is not equivalence; margins should be scientifically justified.
Simple inner-filter correction formulas depend on optical geometry. For f=F_without/F_with, attenuation correction multiplies signal by f, not by 1/f.

The draft reference uses reporter Km as a preparation item, but full reporter Michaelis-Menten characterization is not universally essential if empirical capacity and relevant intermediate concentrations are validated.

No fixed concentrations, replicate counts, Z-prime or R-squared thresholds are supplied by the packet. Proposed pilot settings are acceptable when labeled and validated; they are not historical facts.
